requirements.requirement: On node1, a web service listens on TCP port 8081 and is reachable through the loopback interface.
requirements.summary: Before and after restart, lighttpd was started, listening on 127.0.0.1:8081, and returned HTTP 200 with the expected content through 127.0.0.1.

requirements.requirement: The TCP 8081 web service is not reachable through node1's external interfaces.
requirements.summary: The observed service socket was bound only to 127.0.0.1, while connection attempts to the sole observed external IPv4 address, 10.100.234.10, were refused both before and after restart. No IPv6 port-8081 listener was present.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart service and boot ID, acknowledged the reboot, returned with a different boot ID corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered its service, configuration, content checksum, listener restriction, and HTTP behavior.
limitations: The external-address probes originated on node1 rather than from a separate remote host; the exclusive 127.0.0.1 listener observations strongly corroborate the refusal results.
The generic lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because it checked systemd on Alpine; direct OpenRC status nevertheless showed lighttpd healthy.

operational_hygiene.summary: The package installation, configuration/content changes, OpenRC enablement, service start, and reboot all had clear roles in implementing or verifying the outcome. No unrelated troubleshooting mutations were observed. One minor unnecessary retained mutation occurred: the restart command created /tmp/loopback8081-reboot.log, which remained in the final snapshot and was not used by later evidence collection. The configuration backup had a reasonable rollback purpose. Package health was unchanged, and the only added listener was the required loopback socket.
